source: evidence record, publisher episode_assets id 360 (the PoC the approved script cites); timeline.json is from the same run
rerun: 2026-11-05 re-run printed 32.2 / 3984.8 / 3987.7 ms (rerun-2026-11-05.txt): timer noise of about 10 ms, same rounding (32 ms, about 4 s)
conclusion: In this in-process simulation, the client had the first text after a median 31.8 ms when streaming versus 3974.8 ms buffered and total time was within 5% (3980.7 ms vs 3974.8 ms), so here streaming made the text start sooner, not finish sooner.
setup: in-process simulated generator, 120 words, 33+/-8 ms per token (seed 42), 20 calls per mode run concurrently, buffered = one JSON body at the end, stream = SSE frame per token, in-process byte streams replace the planned HTTP chunked transport (no network), no model think-time before the first token, times are client text-availability (parsed, not rendered), total-time tolerance 5%, first-text gap must exceed 100 ms and 50% of buffered
caveats: These are synthetic, in-process results, not measurements of an AI model, deployed product, localhost HTTP server, or real network.
First text means text parsed by the client, not characters rendered or seen by a user. Any animation illustrates arrival timing rather than measured screen rendering.
The simulation omits model time before the first token, network latency, HTTP behavior, proxy buffering, and browser rendering.
Twenty concurrent calls per mode share runtime scheduling conditions; they are not isolated sequential measurements. The roughly four-second lab duration is consistent with concurrency.
With only 20 calls per mode and a fixed seed, p95 estimates are coarse and generalization is limited.
The 5% threshold is a chosen practical tolerance, not statistical proof that completion times are equivalent.
The 5.9 ms difference does not establish streaming overhead or its cause; scheduling, simulated delays, and measurement variation may contribute.
The first-text improvement is a difference between mode medians, not necessarily the median improvement for paired trials.
The configured tokens are simulated emissions associated with a 120-word answer; they should not be described as a real model's tokenizer units or token throughput.
